description.narrative: Objectives of the intervention The intervention aims to improve policy development in Kosovo by 1.) Improving the capacity of the OPM in relation to policy development; 2.) Improving the capacity of staff with a policy coordination and policy scrutiny function; 3.) Improving policy development capacity at the line ministries.

Premiärministerns kontor har ansökt om finansiering för ett flerårigt stöd för förbättrat policyframtagande i Kosovo under perioden 2016-2019. Förslaget anger en förväntad kostnad av högst 30 000 000 svenska kronor (ca 3 240 000 Euro).
Den föreslagna insatsen ämnar påskynda och förbättra ett faktabaserat policyframtagande i Kosovo, genom att stärka koordineringssekretariatet (GCS) som sitter på premiärministerns kontor (OPM). GCS ansvarar för att förbereda och koordinera policyframtagandet, samt att kvalitetsäkra underligande policyanalys.
Insatsen ämnar förbättra policyframtagandet och koordineringskapaciteten genom att: 1.) Förbättra ramverket för policyframtagande, inklusive riktlinjer och manualer, och säkerställa att det inkluderar konsultationer med allmänheten och kvalitativa former av policyanalys; 2.) Utveckla GCS kapacitet att, i nära samarbete med det strategiska planeringskontoret, långsiktigt planera policyframtagande baserat på policyprioriteringar och linjeministeriernas strategiska planer; 3.) Öka linjeministeriernas kapacitet att bidra till policyframtagande; 4.) Förbättra kommunikation och koordinering under policyframtagandet.
Av den totala budgeten ska högst 8 600 000 SEK (ca 940 000EUR) finansiera projektaktiviteter implementerade av OPM, emedan kvarstående högst 21 400 000 SEK (ca 2 300 000 EUR) ska finansiera teknisk assistans upphandlad av ambassaden. Aktivitetsbudgeten inkluderar medel för projektrevision, en extern halvtidsöversyn och en ex-post utvärdering.

The Office of the Prime Minister has submitted a proposal for a multi-annual support for improving policy development in Kosovo during the period 2016-2019. The proposal outlines expected total costs of max 30 000 000 SEK( 3 240 000 EUR)
The proposed intervention aims to speed up and improve an evidence based policy development system in Kosovo, by strengthening the capacity of the Government Coordination Secretariat (GCS) in the Office of the Prime Minister (OPM). The GCS is responsible for preparing and coordinating the policy development, including quality assurance of underlying policy analysis.
The intervention aims to increase the policy development and coordination capacity by: 1.) Increasing the capacity at the line ministries to improve their input into the policy making process 2.) Developing the GCS’s capacity to, in close collaboration with the Strategic Planning Office (SPO), conduct forward planning for policy development, based on policy priorities and the line ministry’s strategic plan; 3.) Improving the policy development framework, including guidelines and manuals, ensuring an inclusion of public consultations and qualitative forms of policy analysis; and 4.) Improving communication on the policy development framework.
Out of the total budget max 8 600 000 SEK (940 000EUR) will be used for project activities implemented by the OPM while the remainder of max 21 400 000 SEK (2 300 000 EUR) will be used to finance technical assistance procured by the Embassy.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The activities within the program at the Office of the Prime Minister, OPM, ended December 2021 and a completion report was submitted in March 10, 2022. The submission of the report was followed by a meeting to discuss the results and possible impacts for a long run. At that time the above mentioned evaluation was also a good platform for the final dialogue, parallel to meetings with some team members. The last meeting with the project leaders was held Monday 13th of June, 2022. Some correspondance were taking place also during the autumn 2022, for the final closing.
The total budget for the program was originally SEK 30 000 000.
A summery of the results follows, linked to the five main goals of the project:
1) Better regulation strategy. This strategy was not planned in the beginning but became, when finalized, a politically relevant document to provide a strong and broad foundation for the project's work.
2) Guidelines and manual for developing concept documents and standard cost model manual. These were approved by the government in December 2017 and used during the continued period of the program as well as afterwards.
3) Policy communication with strategic work that enhanced the communication within the government and for a better outreach to the public - including public consultation. A redrafting was also done for the sub-legal act regulating public communication - in 2018 - and adopted in December same year after a widely consulting process. Additionally, a handbook is in place for civil servants and communication officers as a technical guide with practical advices.
4) An indicative forward work plan, for a better coordinated planning - with the result of one overall umbrella document. The Government Work Plan, GWP, includes now both the annual projection of activities as well as the indicative overview of activities for two additional years.
5) Concept document and programme on administrative burden reduction which lead to an adoption of a comprehensive programme to scrutinise all laws and sub-legal acts, and assess how these are improving the efficiency regarding administrative procedures. It was adopted on October 19, 2020.
Parallel to the activities in the above areas a range of training programmes - for capacity development - were organized linked to the overall programme with the aim to strengthen the competences for civil servants working within the above mentioned fields. The trainings with experts were conducted by Public Administration International (PAi). During the pandemic the training slow down and it was not possible to carry out all trainings that should continue by trained trainers even though the mission from PAi was ended (end of December 2020), but the team assures in the final report that "the GCS staff (Government civil servants) was not lacking in providing support to the ministries in various forms of meetings and communication".
The final report also highlights the international outreach activities, such as study visits and exchanges with countries like Sweden, Belgium and the Netherlands, Germany, Estonia and Montenegro to learn from other sister organizations regarding policy development. The team also had a close cooperation with Albania in the area of Better Regulation.
The project was rolling without any big obstacles in the first three years. However due to many government shifts and challenges during the pandemic during 2020 and 2021 several obstacles occurred that slowed down the progress of the project.
Another difficulty was brought up in the last meeting between the team leaders and the Embassy; the structure of the Office of the Prime Minister in Kosovo was changed in November 2020. This caused some confusion and difficulties in planning for the project.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
